claims.text: Multi-element, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles can be prepared by physical or chemical synthesis.
Binary phase-diagram analysis can identify compositional regions expected to form single-phase high-entropy-alloy solid solutions.
Falling within a binary-phase-diagram-predicted single-solid-solution region implies a benefit from high configurational entropy.
Nanoparticles within the predicted single-solid-solution region will retain structural and chemical integrity at high temperature better than nanoparticles outside that region.
The relevant catalytic service-temperature range is 773–1173 K.
The relevant thermoelectric service-temperature range is 473–1923 K.
In-zone compositions will retain a homogeneous single-phase structure during high-temperature exposure.
In-zone compositions will avoid elemental segregation during high-temperature exposure.
In-zone compositions will avoid intermetallic formation during high-temperature exposure.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the solid-solution phase in compositions within the predicted stability zone.
Configurational-entropy stabilization slows diffusion-driven phase separation at elevated temperature.
Configurational-entropy stabilization prevents detrimental intermetallic and segregated phases from forming at elevated temperature.
Compositions outside the predicted region have lower entropic stabilization than in-zone compositions.
Compositions outside the predicted region are more prone to phase separation and intermetallic formation.
In-zone nanoparticles will undergo negligible microstructural change and minimal segregation or precipitation after prolonged high-temperature exposure.
In-zone nanoparticles will sustain catalytic or thermoelectric performance after prolonged high-temperature exposure.
Out-of-zone nanoparticles will exhibit phase separation, intermetallic formation, and declining catalytic or thermoelectric performance.
Nanoscale surface segregation, kinetic limitations, and deviations from bulk behavior may shift the predicted stability-region boundaries and alter the magnitude of compositional effects.
